fr.elements: Main Residence; Access Drive; Open Green Space; Dense Vegetation; Detached Structure
fr.considerations: Single Access Point; Long Driveway; Dense Vegetation; Limited Turnaround Space
fr.recommendations:
• Mark the driveway entrance with reflective address numbers visible from both directions on the road.
• Install a turnaround area or marked pull-off near the detached structure or open green space to allow fire and emergency vehicles to reverse direction without backing the full driveway length.
• Trim vegetation along both sides of the driveway to maintain a clear travel width for emergency vehicles.
• Cut back any overhanging branches above the driveway to allow full-height vehicle clearance for fire apparatus.
• Keep the driveway surface clear of parked vehicles, equipment, and debris so the full length remains passable at all times.
• Post the property address at the driveway entrance, not only at the residence, so responders can confirm the correct access point before committing to the long approach.
• Identify and communicate an alternate foot access route through the open green space to the main residence in case the driveway becomes blocked.
• Thin dense vegetation adjacent to the driveway so responders on foot can move between the driveway and the main residence without obstruction.
• Keep the area around the detached structure clear enough for responders to stage equipment without repositioning vehicles.

wildfire.conditions: Structure Surrounded by Vegetation; Scattered Shrubs; Scattered Shrubs; Scattered Shrubs; Scattered Trees; Long Driveway; Vegetation Near Structure; Open Terrain; Scattered Shrubs; Ground Vegetation; Single Access Route; Scattered Shrubs
wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim shrubs growing directly next to the house on all sides.
• Remove ground vegetation within several feet of the house foundation.
• Thin scattered trees near the house to increase open space between the canopy and the structure.
• Separate shrub clusters so they are not continuous from the surrounding terrain toward the house.
• Clear overhanging branches above the driveway to keep the full width passable for vehicles.
• Remove shrubs and ground vegetation growing along the driveway edges that could block or slow vehicle movement.
• Keep the driveway surface clear of dead leaves, branches, and loose plant material.
• Thin shrubs on both sides of the single access route to maintain open sightlines and easy movement along its full length.
• Remove dead or dry ground vegetation from open areas between the house and surrounding shrubs.
• Cut back any shrubs that are touching or leaning against the house walls or roof.
• Maintain a visible, unobstructed path around all sides of the structure.
